title: Alex: promote from within or hire outside (ranges typed on the tree)
story: A head-of-analytics role. Promoting Alex costs 5k of training; Alex thrives (+40k over three years) with a chance put at 40% to 85%, likely 60%, is fine 25% of the time, and otherwise struggles (-60k). An external hire costs 20k to 50k, likely 35k, all-in; the hire is strong (+100k) 45% of the time, average 30%, and poor (-50k) otherwise, in which case they leave in year one half the time and a second search costs 20k. Leaving the role vacant costs 30k. The ranges are typed straight onto the tree, not as shared numbers.
source: Marritt, 'Should you replace Sam?': the replacement as a chance node, and 'A confident, narrow, invented range produces a confident, narrow, invented answer'
what_it_tests: ranges typed into a chance and into an option's value on the tree (anonymous estimates)
three outcomes in a group, with a nested group under one of them
worlds whose chances do not fit: when 'Alex thrives' draws above 75%, the group passes 100%; the share of such worlds is known in closed form
switch-point sweeps that must skip the values where the chances stop fitting
